| n1 | crates/core/src/model.rs:624 and the live-proof AC6 receipt | NOT A DEFECT, RECORDED SO IT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN ACCIDENT. The live receipt now reads `"next_retry_at": 0`, which is correct under the new definition (a fresh row's persisted not_before is 0 = eligible immediately) and the doc comment says so. But the field NAME still spells a wall-clock instant ('_at'), and 0 as Unix milliseconds renders as 1970-01-01 in any consumer that does the obvious thing with it. Absent-vs-0 is decodable on the wire because skip_serializing_if drops the None case, so nothing is ambiguous — the risk is purely that a downstream renderer shows an epoch date for 'now'. Cheap options if it ever bites: report max(not_before_ms, now) so the value is always a real instant, or name the field for the eligibility it now carries. No action needed for plan 133. |
| n2 | crates/tmux/src/lib.rs:395-410 | TWO PROPERTIES OF THE NEW WRITER PROBE WORTH KNOWING, NEITHER BLOCKING. (1) It shells out to `ps -axo command=` on every adoption of a piped unmarked pane. macOS ps can truncate long command lines; the sinks here are ~57 characters and well clear, but a deeply nested HOME would fail the substring match and the check fails CLOSED (refuse to supersede), so the failure direction is the safe one — it would break AC1 loudly, never AC3 silently. (2) The match is a substring test, which is safe against pane-id prefix collisions only because of the `.raw` suffix: `_31.raw` is not a substring of `_317.raw`. That is load-bearing and undocumented; if the sink naming ever loses its extension the probe starts matching the wrong pane. |
